slides.0.title: VCP and the label
slides.0.subtitle: Decree 283/993 of 1993
slides.1.title: Two categories
slides.1.highlights.0.title: VCP
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Decree 283/993 of 16 June 1993: a Vino de Calidad Preferente must be made from Vitis vinifera varieties of recognised quality accepted by INAVI (then called the INV), which keeps the list
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Vino Común
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine that does not meet these requirements and is not VCP must be labelled "Vino Común", in letters as tall as the VCP wording
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Glass bottles only
slides.1.highlights.2.content: VCP may only be sold in glass bottles of at most 750 ml; INAVI may set smaller sizes
slides.1.content: VCP is the quality term you will meet most often on Uruguayan labels.
slides.2.title: VCP's analytical limits
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Alcohol
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Volatile acidity
slides.2.highlights.1.content: At most 0.80 g/L, expressed as sulphuric acid; above 12% alcohol, 0.04 g/L more is allowed per extra degree
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Sulphur dioxide
slides.2.highlights.2.content: At most 200 mg/L in wine under 4 g/L of sugar and 300 mg/L above that. The wine must also pass stability tests and show no sensory faults
slides.2.content: Article 4 sets four requirements; article 5 allows exceptions on the advice of the oenological committee.
slides.3.title: Rules for the label
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Mandatory items
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Country, maker or bottler, INAVI registration number, type of wine, alcohol, and the words "Vino de Calidad Preferente (VCP)", at least 6 mm tall on a 750 ml bottle
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Variety: 85%
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A named variety must make up at least 85%. Two varieties may be named if together they make 100%. The wording comes from Decree 325/997 of 1997
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Vintage: 85%
slides.3.highlights.2.content: A stated vintage requires all or at least 85% of the wine to come from that year. Labels must be approved and registered by INAVI, which refuses misleading place names
slides.3.content: Variety, vintage and place are optional, but once stated they must follow the rules.
